went_well.description: One sentence of at most 25 words: the one thing they did best on this run and why it matters, backed by a specific split or effort quoted exactly as written (say whether a pace is actual or allowing for the hill). Judge on `flat` and use `gain`/`loss` to say whether a split was uphill, downhill or rolling. Must be true of the data; no generic praise.

work_on.description: One sentence of at most 30 words: the single most important thing to improve, shown by a specific split quoted exactly as written, and a concrete way to do it on the next runs (for example hold back the first kilometre to a given pace). Must agree with `run.shape`. Check every split before calling a stretch consistent.

result.description: One sentence of at most 25 words comparing today's standard-distance effort with the target and previous best, quoting `eff` times and differences exactly as written (e.g. 30:51, 3:51 off your 27:00 target). On a first run (`hist.runs` 0) call it a baseline. If there is no target and no previous best, describe what today sets as their benchmark.

forecast.description: Your prediction of what this runner will actually do on their next run, judged from their own history (`recent`, `wk`, `hist.rest_d`), not from what you prescribed in `next`. It is scored against the run they really log next.

km.description: The distance in km you expect them to actually run next time, based on the distances they usually choose.

pace.description: The average pace you expect for that run, as "m:ss" (never a range), allowing for their recent form, how often they run easy, and any trend in `recent`. Just the time, no units.
